summary: This bill amends the Higher Education Act to bar colleges from requiring students, employees, or applicants to endorse race-based ideological statements or submit diversity/equity/inclusion-related statements, and from giving preferential treatment based on such statements.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Higher Education Act to add conditions for institutional participation in federal student aid programs but does not authorize, expand, or reduce any appropriations or government outlays. It is a regulatory restriction only.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
The legislation is confined to higher-education admissions and employment practices; it contains nothing related to health coverage, insurance markets, or medical care delivery.
No references to firearms, Second Amendment issues, or gun regulations appear in the bill.
The bill does not alter immigration law, visas, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.
No language concerns reproductive rights, abortion access, or funding restrictions.
Defense spending levels and military policy are untouched by this higher-education measure.
Environmental regulations, climate policy, and conservation measures are outside the bill’s scope.
Welfare programs, SNAP, Medicaid eligibility, or other safety-net entitlements are not addressed.

The bill directly amends the Higher Education Act to prohibit institutions receiving federal student-aid funds from requiring diversity, equity, and inclusion statements or ideological endorsements related to race and ethnicity. This constitutes federal regulatory intervention in higher-education admissions and hiring practices, thereby engaging the education topic, though it does not address K-12 funding, school choice mechanisms, or privatization.
No provisions relate to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
Sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal procedure are not mentioned.
Tariffs, trade agreements, and globalization measures are absent.
The bill neither authorizes new spending nor contains deficit-reduction provisions.
The text focuses exclusively on race, color, ethnicity, and national origin; it does not address sexual orientation or gender identity protections.
Foreign assistance programs are outside the bill’s domestic higher-education focus.
Voter access, election administration, and campaign finance are not implicated.
Data privacy, technology regulation, and surveillance issues are not addressed.
Union rights, collective bargaining, and worker protections receive no mention.

While the bill bars compelled ideological statements, it expressly preserves an institution’s ability to require certification of compliance with federal and state antidiscrimination laws. The net effect on the balance between religious exemptions and civil-rights enforcement is therefore negligible.
